Want to add them https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Decorator/ManagedHost.interface.yaml#L11 here too?
Shouldn't this be contained_by like DIMM ?
I think this is wrong based on https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/83773/34/redfish-core/lib/processor.hpp

Not sure you need bmcweb, I don't understand why these are mandatory? 
Not sure what the Item.Board / Item.Chassis is about? 

Does soemthing like below work ?

Optionally implement the contained_by association to provide links to Cpus and Dimms. These associations are used for finding Dimms and Cpus of the managed host computer system.

Why is it required? If you want your processors out on Redfish, etc. Yep, you need this association. Does something like below work for a start?

   Objects that implement Cpu can optionally implement the contained_by association to provide links to ManagedHost.

Huh? Why shouldn't this be of type Inventory.Decorator.ManagedHost? 
What does Item.Board or Item.Chassis have to do with this?
I don't understand the Item.Board or Item.Chassis thing here?

I've generally taken the philosophy that we should use the generic Inventory.Item rather than using the specific ones.  I find that for these someone later on will add another and another and it is of low value to have the specifics here.

Is there a strong reason why we want to be explicit of {Cpu, Dimm} in this case or can we put this on the generic association?
I have no opinion on that. @gunnar@gmills.xyz maybe?

> Is there a strong reason why we want to be explicit of {Cpu, Dimm} in this case or can we put this on the generic association?

Not sure if that counts as a strong reason, but

If we were to put
```
required_endpoint_interfaces:
          - xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item
```

we are effectively saying that 

```
xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.PCIeFunction
xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.Chassis
xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.CpuCore
xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.NetworkInterface
...
```

can be `contained_by` a ManagedHost, right?

Otherwise we are documenting an association which will not even be used or implemented.

### Ambiguity in querying

Something like bmcweb needs to know which associations can and should be used to query things on DBus.

With how the associations are currently documented on `xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item`

https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/900af2c70e9c045508f60c029583b6cc30eb596a/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Item.interface.yaml

it may not be entirely clear. How do we find the powersupplies for a chassis?
Do we go with `contained_by` and look for `Inventory.Item.PowerSupply`?

Do we go with `powered_by` instead?

For powersupplies this is solved since `Inventory.Item.Chassis` documents a `powered_by` association **specifically** to `Inventory.Item.PowerSupply`.

### PDI should be source of truth for how to query associations

If we do not document these associations in a fine grained manner in PDI, bmcweb will effectively take over this role and the associations will have to be created in such a way that it aligns with how bmcweb is querying them.

Do we want that?

### In terms of the concrete example

How do we find `Inventory.Item.Dimm` when starting from a ManagedHost?

If we specify `containing` `Inventory.Item` then it may be unclear if that is directly leading us to `Inventory.Item.Dimm` or if there is another inventory item in-between that must be queried.

Maybe the `oontaining` for `Inventory.Item` there is meant for `Inventory.Item.Cpu` and `Inventory.Item.Dimm` is queried in some other way?

All these questions may pop up.

Reactors and external interfaces may need the fine grained documentation there to know which associations to create where and how to query.

We also could go with `xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.System` rather than `xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Decorator.ManagedHost`. 
 
`Inventory.Item.System` is also used to identify objects as computer systems and not specific to multi-host. Ideally we use interfaces, that are configured on both single- and multi-host, considering that long term we should use associations for both platform types.

In that case we would need to make some smaller adjustments in EM and bmcweb for multi-host, like adding `Inventory.Item.System` to the multi-host configs, as well as including the interface in our dbus queries in bmcweb.

> it may not be entirely clear. How do we find the powersupplies for a chassis? Do we go with contained_by and look for Inventory.Item.PowerSupply? Do we go with powered_by instead?  For powersupplies this is solved since Inventory.Item.Chassis documents a powered_by association specifically to Inventory.Item.PowerSupply.

1. It entirely depends on what you're trying to deduce.  Are you looking for the power supply *in* a chassis or a power supply *powering* a chassis?  These are two different associations because they're two different inquiries.

2. If you are suggesting we also change powered_by to be on Item, feel free to go for it.

> PDI should be source of truth for how to query associations.
> If we do not document these associations in a fine grained manner in PDI, bmcweb will effectively take over this role and the associations will have to be created in such a way that it aligns with how bmcweb is querying them.

PDI being a source of truth does not imply a requirement on it documenting fine grained associations.

PDI is being truthful: any Item may be "contained in" a Chassis.  Just because bmcweb, entity-manager, etc. do not **implement** a complete set does not mean it isn't a **reasonable** association; one which might be leveraged in the future without any further design discussion.

> How do we find Inventory.Item.Dimm when starting from a ManagedHost?

This same question has been posed when I wrote the association requirements that we would not accept associations like "dimm_contained_in_chassis".  Anytime you have two potential interfaces using the same association you may need to further deduce which ones are what.  There's fundamentally nothing in PDI that prevents you from formulating a "GPU Card" as an { Item, Asset, Board, CPU, and DIMM } all in one dbus path.

If you want these kinds of queries to be more efficient, I would suggest we improve the mapper query APIs.

> We also could go with xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.System rather than xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Decorator.ManagedHost.

I'm fine with this also.  Do we have `Item.System` implemented everywhere necessary though?  It doesn't appear that any Meta configs currently expose `Item.System`.

I removed the specific Item type from ManagedHost interface in accordance to your first comment. No need to broaden the discussion about the use of `Item.System` in place of `ManagedHost`. 

@patrick@stwcx.xyz let me know if there is anything else. My roadmap is to resolve this so I can get the bmcweb changes host hw-inventory in until chistmas.
Marking this as resolved. Parts of the discussion above ventured into conceptual design of associations and in my opinion this tangible change is the wrong place to resolve these questions.
